newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle ranged from 0.400 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower while feeder cattle indications ranged 0.200 higher to 0.200 lower, livestock analysts said.

Bull spreading is expected to dominate live cattle futures at the start following Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed Report. Active marketings last month were considered bullish to nearbys while the continued heavy placement pace is generally bearish to deferreds, analysts said.
The report showed May marketings at 104 percent of last year, or 1.8 million head, a record for the month.
Expectations boxed beef prices are near a bottom and that packers may pay $63 to $64 per cwt for fed cattle this week were also cited as supportive factors, analysts and traders said.

Feeder cattle futures may take part of their cue from live cattle. Active marketings recently could encourage continued good demand for replacement feeders at feedlots. Lower corn futures indictions were also supportive, they said.
However, a lower CME feeder cattle index and possibly lower prices in deferred live cattle may weigh on the market, traders added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.45 at $76.74 per cwt.
